pr_title: [mono] Reintroduce an internal Marshal class method used by the runtime
pr_comments: On local testing this still fails, but I am suspecting a problem with System.Private.CoreLib.dll not being updated for the CoreCLR tests after a rebuild. I have rebased and enabled the tests on CI to see if this can clear up what's going on.
The CoreCLR runtime tests are currently not running properly on Mono, so this looks like it is passing several tests which it doesn't in the "Mono Pri0 Test Run" lane
With the linker descriptor added, this patch now passes the failing tests on Mono and should be good to merge.
@EgorBo @akoeplinger can you think of a reason the test is failing on CI but not locally anymore?

@alexischr the stackoverflow test is a known issue that is fixed by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/35812. you can rebase/merge master to get the fix for that.

I assume you're talking about ICustomMarshaler.sh ?
@akoeplinger Yeah, I think I see now - I was running the _other_ failing test locally accidentally, and that one's fixed
@akoeplinger Yeah. With a rebase, even the ICustomMarshaler failure seems to have gone from the Mono Pri0 Test run..? Could you please confirm?
Yeah right now, only the helix step seems to be failing. @naricc Is that expected?

@alexischr   The way test failures show up is confusing. They will all show up as a failure in the send to helix step. To see the actual test failures in a nice way, click on the build ID, and the click "tests". In this case that brings you here:

https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/public/_build/results?buildId=632049&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab

In this case it is the ICustomMarshaller test failing.

The "Interop Work Item" just means some test in the Interop group is failing; not too helpful.

comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. Please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

CoreCLR [PR](https://github.com/dotnet/coreclr/pull/21606) and [issue](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/10965) prompting this test, though they aren't what's directly causing the crash here.

The problematic line is this, as that method does not exist in our netcore implementation of Marshal:
```
		get_instance = get_method_nofail (Marshal, "GetCustomMarshalerInstance", 2, 0);
```

I assume the Marshal managed implementation changed to use more shared code but the native side wasn't updated to reflect that. I'm not sure what all the changes were or how much the native side needs adjustment.

review_comments:
isn't the whole block should be under `lock` ? otherwise it might be executed twice.
Also I guess you can lock on `MarshalerInstanceCache` without a separate lock object (which introduces a static constructor) since `LazyInitializer.EnsureInitialized` is thread-safe.
Yup, the code should have extended the lock across the uses of MarshalerInstanceCache, not just when getting/setting. I will do that
AFAICT this would only potentially cause churn from misuse of the cache and not actual bad state.

@EgorBo hm now I am not sure if I want to "fix" this: it seems valid to avoid a potentially long wait, with the cost of some cache misses/un-needed cache refreshes/heap churn. 

I will remove the separate lock object though.
@jkotas is there coreclr implementation we could cheaply use instead?
I do not think so. All interop generation is C++ in CoreCLR.
CoreCLR doesn't seem to use this, but some of our tests' .config files are. At least it seems benign to me to have this catch block.
